public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 31

The WOWII page records this as **Chung's theorem**. This radius bound is proved
in Section 2 of P. Erdős, M. Saks, and V. T. Sós, *Maximum Induced Trees in
Graphs*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B **41** (1986), 61–79; the authors credit
Fan Chung for the proof. We state it here as a theorem; the formal proof is left
as `sorry` pending a Lean port of the argument.

Here $\mathrm{path}(G)$ is the maximum number of vertices in an induced path,
and $\mathrm{rad}(G)$ is the graph radius.

*References:*
- [E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
- [P. Erdős, M. Saks, V. T. Sós, Maximum Induced Trees in Graphs](https://doi.org/10.1016/0095-8956(86)90028-6)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture31

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 31](http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html#conj31)
(Chung):

For every simple connected graph $G$,
$\mathrm{path}(G) \ge 2 \cdot \mathrm{rad}(G) - 1$,
where $\mathrm{path}(G)$ is the maximum number of vertices in an induced path
and $\mathrm{rad}(G)$ is the graph radius.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/wowii-graph-conjecture-31-lean/blob/a948e9fc07e11b786aee8dadb1376b4d938454d6/lean/GraphConjecture31.lean"]
theorem conjecture31 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected) :
    2 * (G.radius.toNat : ℤ) - 1 ≤ (path G : ℤ) := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The `path G` invariant cast to ℤ is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ (path G : ℤ) := Int.natCast_nonneg _

/-- The radius cast to ℤ is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ (G.radius.toNat : ℤ) := Int.natCast_nonneg _

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture31

reformulations.difference: Lean assumes [Nontrivial α], whereas the sources state the bound for every connected graph without explicitly excluding a singleton.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An empty graph is not connected. A connected graph with a subsingleton vertex type has radius zero, so the inequality becomes -1 ≤ (path G : ℤ), which holds automatically. Thus restricting to at least two vertices loses no mathematical content. A universe-polymorphic equivalence between the restricted and unrestricted universal statements was proved in Review.nontrivial_restriction_equiv in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the conjecture.

sources_consulted: E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 31 and adjacent variant 31a: https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161800id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html#conj31

P. Erdős, M. Saks, V. T. Sós, Maximum Induced Trees in Graphs, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 41 (1986), 61–79, definitions on p. 62 and Theorem 2.2 with its proof on pp. 64–65. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/0095-8956(86)90028-6; paper read at https://real.mtak.hu/110576/1/1-s2.0-0095895686900286-main.pdf
Collected Papers of Paul Erdős, bibliographic entry 1986-08: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html
Local definitions: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/VertexDistance.lean, especially isInducedPath and path.
Local computational radius definitions and correctness theorem: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Eccentricity.lean.
Local Mathlib sources: Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Diam.lean, Metric.lean, Connectivity/Connected.lean, and Data/ENat/Basic.lean.
review.notes: Checked the main theorem and both sanity-check examples. The source's path invariant counts vertices, matching SimpleGraph.path. Scratch proofs verify its maximal-witness semantics and its values on empty, singleton, two-vertex complete, and small path graphs. Finiteness and connectivity imply G.radius ≠ ⊤, so radius.toNat never invokes its infinity-to-zero default in the theorem. The research solved tag agrees with WOWII and the 1986 paper. The exact linked external proof compiled successfully against the supplied Mathlib; its theorem has the same statement and depends only on [propext, choice, Quot.sound], with no sorryAx. The original WOWII site was unavailable, but its archived statement and the primary paper settled the comparison.
